description.narrative:
Insatsens övergriande mål: "Improving disaster preparedness for early and effective response and resilience of communities affected by natural and man-made disasters in territories with high rates of social violence in Nicaraguan Caribbean Coast and El Salvador dry corridor."
Insatsens specifika mål: "Increase early preparedness and response capacity with a focus on protection, gender (with special attention in Sexual and Gender Based Violence) and inclusion of People with Disabilities (PwD), of local actors such as schools and community committees in coordination with national system institutions upon the adverse threats of climate change and social violence in Puerto Cabezas in Nicaragua; Cabañas and Cuscatlán in El Salvador."

Plan International Sverige har ansökt om finansiering av egeninsats om 1 164 706 SEK för EU-projektet "Enabling resilience and disaster preparedness to natural hazards and social violence for high-risk communities in Nicaragua and El Salvador" under 2020-2021.
Insatsen syftar till att:
1. "Improving disaster preparedness for early and effective response and resilience of communities affected by natural and man-made disasters in territories with high rates of social violence in Nicaraguan Caribbean Coast and El Salvador dry corridor."
2. "Increase early preparedness and response capacity with a focus on protection, gender (with special attention in Sexual and Gender Based Violence) and inclusion of People with Disabilities (PwD), of local actors such as schools and community committees in coordination with national system institutions upon the adverse threats of climate change and social violence in Puerto Cabezas in Nicaragua; Cabañas and Cuscatlán in El Salvador."
Projektet kommer att genomföras på regional nivå i El Salvador och Plan International Sverige kommer att arbeta i samverkan med Plan International El Salvador. Projektet är även nära samordnat med utbildningsministeriet i El Salvador. Plan International Sverige är huvudsökande organisation och har det övergripande ansvaret för projektets implementering och koordinering.
Den aktuella insatsen har EU-kommissionens referensnummer ECHO/-AM/BUD/2020/91000. Insatsen har en total budget på 705 882, 35 EUR, vilket motsvarar cirka 7 517 882 SEK. Av detta har Plan International beviljats 600 000 EUR från EU-kommissionen och ansöker om 1 164 706 SEK (cirka 15%) från Sida.
Insatsen innebär en sammanslagning av två projekt under ett avtal. Plan International Sverige ansvarar för den del av insatsen som implementeras i El Salvador och ansökan omfattar bara den delen av projektet. Plan International Spanien ansvarar i sin tur för den del av insatsen som implementeras i Nicaragua. Insatsen har två specifika mål för respektive land samt ett gemensamt mål för båda i form av en krismodifierare. Insatsen i El Salvador och Nicaragua innebär två separata budgetar.
Eftersom Plan International Spanien är avtalspart till ECHO ställer Sida som krav att ett avtal mellan Plan International Spanien och Plan International Sverige upprättas innan Sida betalar ut medel.

Plan International Sweden has applied to Sida for funding of 1 164 706 SEK to carry out the EU-project "Enabling resilience and disaster preparedness to natural hazards and social violence for high-risk communities in Nicaragua and El Salvador" during 2020-2021.
The project aims to:
1. "Improving disaster preparedness for early and effective response and resilience of communities affected by natural and man-made disasters in territories with high rates of social violence in Nicaraguan Caribbean Coast and El Salvador dry corridor."
2. "Increase early preparedness and response capacity with a focus on protection, gender (with special attention in Sexual and Gender Based Violence) and inclusion of People with Disabilities (PwD), of local actors such as schools and community committees in coordination with national system institutions upon the adverse threats of climate change and social violence in Puerto Cabezas in Nicaragua; Cabañas and Cuscatlán in El Salvador."
The project will be conducted on a regional level in El Salvador, and Plan International Sweden will collaborate with Plan International El Salvador. The project is also closely coordinated with the Ministry of Education in El Salvador. Plan International Sweden is lead applicant to Sida and has the overall responsibility for the coordination and implementation of the project.
The contribution has the EU Commission reference number: ECHO/-AM/BUD/2020/91000. The contribution's total budget is 705 882 EUR, which corresponds to approximately 7 517 882 SEK. The requested support from Sida is 1 164 706 SEK, which corresponds to 15% of the total budget.
ECHO asked Plan International to merge two projects under one contract. Plan International Sweden is responsible for the part of the action being implemented in El Salvador and this match application is only in regards to that part of the action. Plan International Spain is responsible for the part of the action being implemented in Nicaragua. The action has two specific results for Nicaragua and El Salvador respectively and a joint result in the form of a crisis modifier. ECHO allocated a specific budget amount to the El Salvador and Nicaragua part of the action respectively.
Due to Plan International Spain being the agreement partner to ECHO, a condition for the first payment will be that an agreement between Plan International Spain and Plan International Sweden is signed and sent to Sida.

- "The action was implemented in communities that are part of the governments Territorial Control Plan i.e. territories with the higher levels of social violence and vulnerability in El Salvador, which limits mobility and ability to organize. Under this action, Plan International was the implementing entity working directly with the project rights holders and members of the local formal and informal civil society to strengthen resilience towards natural disasters and social violence as well as hold duty bearers accountable for providing a safe environment within schools and the community at large and allow children and young people to return to school".
- "Through the comprehensive safe schools framework, the project established capacity building of the so-called School Protection Commissions, in order to provide timely response to emergencies caused by natural hazards and social violence. A total of 15 school protection committees were formed, trained and equipped in 15 schools. To ensure the sustainability and generational change of the Commissions, parents, caregivers, teachers and directors were included in the committees as participants in a smaller proportion than students. The committees actively participated in the trainings such as development of risks, capacities and resource maps, as well as in the preparation of their school protection plans. Plan International's Safe Schools Model has been used. The model aligns with the Comprehensive Safe Schools Framework promoted by The Global Alliance for Disaster Risk Reduction and Resilience in the Education Sector".
- "The action supported a range of structures within the targeted schools and the communities in order to identify meeting places for local civil society actors and other duty bearers and community members. These structures provide a mechanism for collaboration between CSO, duty bearers and communities, fostering the relationship building and creating a space for dialogue, by contributing to create an enabling environment for civil society to operate".
